key_insight: The paper shows that autonomous LiDAR-informed 3D mapping can fuse RGB and thermal views to inspect hard-to-see under-panel solar farm components, not just module surfaces.
engineering_relevance: This enables scalable, spatially grounded fault detection for connectors, cabling, and structural hardware in utility-scale PV plants, improving maintenance targeting and traceability.
method: LiDAR-inertial SLAM reconstructs the 3D solar-farm environment.
Geometrically calibrated RGB and thermal images are fused across viewpoints.
Machine-learning detectors and segmenters localize components, then link anomalies to specific 3D assets.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports utility-scale PV demonstrations for MC4 connector detection and connection-state recognition, thermal anomaly identification, and detection of bolts, nuts, and torque tubes.
watch_item: Performance may depend on accurate calibration, sufficient viewpoint coverage, and reliable localization in the visually repetitive and partially occluded under-array environment.
paper_title: Autonomous 3D Visual-Thermal Inspection for Utility-Scale Solar Farms
